name: QB draw
seenIn: Covered in Football 101, Lesson 33: Quarterback runs: designed runs, scrambles and sneaks (and how to log each in your drill)
what: The QB draw is a run play dressed up as a pass. The quarterback, usually in the shotgun, takes the snap and looks like he's about to throw, then tucks the ball and runs straight up the middle himself.

Everyone sells the pass for a beat: the linemen set up like they're pass blocking, the receivers run routes, and the linebackers read "pass" and drop back into coverage. That empties the middle of the field. Then the running back turns into a lead blocker through the A gap (beside the center) and the quarterback follows him into the space the linebackers just left.

Teams call it on passing downs against defenses that rush hard and drop their linebackers deep, and it's a favorite with mobile quarterbacks because the QB is an extra ball carrier the defense has to account for.

caption: Solid white: receivers' routes, the running back's lead block and the quarterback's path up the middle right behind the back. Yellow dashes: the linebackers dropping into coverage, which opens the middle.
spot: Shotgun, often on 2nd or 3rd and medium-to-long. At the snap the QB looks downfield and the line pass-sets like any pass play, but the running back steps up into the line instead of out to a route, and a moment later the QB tucks the ball and runs right behind him. Unlike a scramble, it happens fast and through the middle, before the pocket has broken down.
beats: Defenses that rush the passer hard upfield and drop their linebackers into deep coverage, especially on passing downs. Log it as a Run in the drill: it was called as a run, even though it looks like a pass at the snap.
